THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 13.11.2014 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. M.A.C.T., Holalkere ('the Tribunal' in short) in M.V.C.No.156/2013.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 08.12.2011 at about 07:30 pm while the petitioner was riding the NC: 2023:KHC:33617 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-16/W-0222 from Somasundara Village towards Srirampura Village near the land of Pandurangappa, from the opposite direction a tractor-trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-16- TA/559-560 hit against the motor cycle, injuring him all over the body.

After taking treatment at P.H.C., Hosadurga and S.S. Institure of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, Davanagere for about 23 days, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation.

entities.text: S.S. Institure of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, Davanagere
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The claim was opposed by owner of the tractor.
After taking evidence, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,01,000/- with 8% interest by the impugned judgment.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri. N.K. Siddeswara, learned counsel for the petitioner.

sentences.text: Service of notice in respect of respondent No.2 is held sufficient.

5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered fracture of left tibia, he was hospitalized for about 23 days, he has been treated by surgeons and damaged one testicle of petitioner was removed.
Because of this, the petitioner went into depression, subjected to enormous pain and suffering and discomfort.
The Tribunal has not properly assessed the compensation.
What has been awarded is disproportionate to the injury and sought for enhancement.
6. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the petitioner and also perused the materials on record.
7. The accident in question is not in dispute.
Ex. P4
/ wound
certificate points out that the petitioner NC: 2023:KHC:33617 has suffered lacerated wound at right side of perineal region extending from the abdomen to 13 cm towards back.
He has suffered fracture of lower left tibia.

Ex.P6 is the discharge summary issued by S.S. Institure of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, Davanagere to the effect that the petitioner was hospitalized for 22 days from 09.12.2011 to 30.12.2011 and it also explains scrotal injury with testicular injury with distal 2/3rd fracture of left tibia.

entities.text: S.S. Institure of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, Davanagere
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Dr. Nitin.
A.B, the Plastic Surgeon operated the petitioner for removal of one testicle.
PW-2 Dr. Nagbhushan.
D.M, though he is not a treated doctor, his evidence points out the injury sustained by the petitioner and also issuing of disability certificate as per Ex.P14 and 15.
The disability certificate is issued by PW-3, who is a treated doctor.
From the medical evidence, it is noticed that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability of 30% of his earning capacity.

If the NC:
2023:KHC:33617 evidence of PW-2 is considered that he was not a treated doctor, we cannot much rely upon Ex.P14.

Ex .P15 is the certificate issued by a treated doctor, points out disability of 19%
because of absence of testis and chronic pain of moderate degree.
I am not persuaded by the evidence of PW-3 and also Ex.P15/disability certificate that the absence of one testicle caused him 19% disability to the petitioner.
As noticed from the medical evidence, the petitioner suffered fracture of left tibia, the Court can make assessment the percentage of disability.
If the evidence of PWs.2 and 3 and Exs.P14 and 15 to be accepted, Court has to determine the disability of the petitioner to the extent of 49%.
The petitioner is a married person having wife and children.
He has enjoyed his life as he is already aged 36 years.

Loss of testicle may cause discomfort and psychological effect, but the fracture of left tibia will certainly cause disability and in the facts and circumstances, I NC: 2023:KHC:33617 am considered that the petitioner has sustained 10% whole body disability.

9. The petitioner claims that he was an Agriculturist and working as Reporter in 'Hosa Digantha'
daily newspaper.
For continuing the agriculture, the injury may cause him discomfort.
Even now, he can report to the newspaper.
The petitioner claims the income of Rs.15,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any proof of income.
The accident took place on 08.12.2011.
A person with no proof of income is assessed not less than Rs.6,500/- per month.
Whereas, the Tribunal has globally awarded Rs.50,000/- towards disability, which is not proper.

As we assessed the percentage of disability, the income of the petitioner at Rs.6,500/-, loss of income due to disability has to be calculated by Kachapurada Rangappa vs K.T. Kanive Rangappa Since Dead By His ... on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155715786/

sentences.text: , then loss of income due to disability will be Rs.6,500/- + NC: 2023:KHC:33617 Rs.2,600/- (40%) = Rs.9,100/- x 12 x 15 x 10% = Rs.1,63,800/-.
Ex.P12 is the medical bills amounting to Rs.57,869/- and the Tribunal has reimbursed the same in total.
The petitioner was hospitalized for 23 days and therefore, attendant charges of Rs.5,000/- has to be assessed.

Towards pain and suffering, a sum of Rs.40,000/-,
towards loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.40,000/-, travelling expenses of Rs.2,000/-, food and nourishment of Rs.10,000/- is also assessed.
The petitioner was laid-up for 4 months.
Hence, a sum of Rs.26,000/- (Rs.6,500/- x 4) as loss of income during laid-up.
Having regard to the testicle injury, the petitioner requires future medical treatment, hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is assessed.
The petitioner is already married, enjoyed his marital life having children.
Hence, there is no ground for assessing compensation of marital loss as assessed by the Tribunal.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to compensation under following heads:
NC: 2023:KHC:33617 Sl. No. Particulars Rs.
1
Pain and sufferings 40,000 2
Medical expenses 57,869 3 Attendant charges 5,000 4
Food and nourishment 10,000 5 Travelling expenses 2,000 6 Loss of amenities and discomfort 40,000 7
Future medical expenses 25,000 8
Loss of income during laid-up 26,000 period (4 months) 9 Loss of income due to disability 1,63,800

The total compensation comes to Rs.3,69,669/- as against Rs.2,01,000/-,
thereby enhancement of Rs.1,68,669/-.
This is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii) Impugned judgment and award is modified.

iii) The petitioner is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,68,669/- with interest of 6% p.a.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:33617 iv) The respondents are directed to deposit the same within eight weeks of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
v) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
